**1. Introduction**

This Project Management Plan (PMP) defines the scope, budget, governance, and control
arrangements for the delivery of Package 7 of the Thameslink Gateway Programme. The
works comprise the following principal elements:

- Utility diversions (gas, water, telecoms) along the A2 corridor between Old Kent Road and
  New Cross Gate.
- Construction of a new pedestrian footbridge at Deptford Church Street.
- Highway realignment and resurfacing works at the junction of Evelyn Street and Rotherhithe
  New Road.
- Ancillary drainage works and environmental mitigation planting.

The contract is administered under the NEC3 Engineering and Construction Contract Option A
(Priced Contract with Activity Schedule). The contract number for all correspondence,
valuations, and change control is MCC-TGP7-2022-001. This number is to be quoted on all
submissions to the Project Controls team and in all correspondence with the client.

**2. Governance Structure**

The project will be managed through a tiered governance structure. The Project Board meets
monthly, chaired by the Project Director, and is attended by the Construction Director, Project
Controls Manager, and the Client PM. The board is responsible for strategic direction, major
change approval, and resolution of issues escalated from the weekly delivery meetings.

Weekly delivery meetings are chaired by the Construction Director and attended by the Site
Agents, Design Lead, and the health and safety advisor. These meetings review progress
against the two-week lookahead, identify potential delays, and allocate resources.

A separate commercial meeting, chaired by the Project Controls Manager, is held fortnightly.
This meeting reviews cost forecasts, compensation events, and the activity schedule.

Delegated authorities are as follows:

- Change Orders up to £25,000: Construction Director
- Change Orders up to £100,000: Project Director

The engagement strategy is based on the power/interest grid. High-power, high-interest

Low-power, low-interest stakeholders are monitored.

- Actual costs to date, by work package and cost code.
- Committed costs (purchase orders and subcontract agreements).
- Forecast final cost, based on the latest information.
- Variance analysis against the approved budget.
- Accruals and prepayments.
- A cash flow forecast for the next three months.

All costs are recorded in the project accounting system (COINS). Direct costs are coded
to the relevant work package. Indirect costs (site overheads, temporary facilities, and
management time) are coded to a separate overhead cost centre and are apportioned to work
packages on a monthly basis using the agreed allocation method.

**7.0 QUALITY MANAGEMENT**

**7.1 General Approach**

The Quality Management System (QMS) for Thameslink Gateway Package 7 is
established in accordance with the project Quality Manual (ref. TGP-QM-001,
Rev 3) and the requirements of the contract. The package is delivered under
a quality regime that ensures all works are planned, executed, and verified
in line with the specified standards.

The key principles of the quality approach are:

- Prevention of non-conformity through clear work instructions and
  briefing.
- Inspection and testing at defined hold points.
- Traceability of materials and workmanship through the lifetime record.
- Prompt reporting and correction of any non-conformance.

The Project Manager holds overall accountability for quality on the
package. Day-to-day assurance is delegated to the Site Agent and the
package Quality Advisor (QA), who reports to the Project Manager on a
functional basis.

**7.2 Quality Manual and Policies**

The Quality Manual defines the framework for all quality-related
activities. Where any conflict arises between this Project Management
Plan and the Quality Manual, the Quality Manual takes precedence.

**7.3 Inspection and Testing Plans (ITPs)**

Inspection and Test Plans are prepared for each defined work activity or
trade package. Each ITP identifies:

- The activity or installation step.
- The inspection or test to be carried out.
- The acceptance criteria, with reference to the specification or
  standard.
- The responsible person for carrying out and witnessing the check.
- The hold point (H) or witness point (W) designation, where applicable.
- The record to be produced as evidence of completion.

ITPs are numbered sequentially within the package (e.g., ITP-001, ITP-002)
and are subject to review and approval by the client’s representative
before work commences on the associated activity.

ITPs are reviewed at least monthly and whenever there is a change in
methodology, a design change, or a recurring non-conformance on the

**7.4 Non-Conformance Reporting**

A non-conformance is any failure to meet a specified requirement. All
non-conformances are recorded on a Non-Conformance Report (NCR) form
(ref. TGP-F-014) and logged in the package NCR register.

The process for managing a non-conformance is as follows:

1. Identification of the non-conformance by any member of the site or
   project team.
2. Raising of the NCR and notification to the Site Agent and the Project
   Controls Manager.
3. Quarantine of the affected product or area, where applicable.
4. Review by the QA and the relevant discipline engineer to determine the
   extent of the non-conformance.
5. Disposition of the non-conformance, which may be:
   - Rework to conform to the specified requirement.
   - Repair with supporting justification and client acceptance.
   - Use as-is with a concession from the client.
   - Rejection and replacement of the item.
6. Implementation of the disposition and verification of completion.
7. Analysis of the root cause and implementation of corrective action to
   prevent recurrence.
**8. Progress Reporting**

Progress reporting is undertaken at three levels: the site weekly
meeting, the package monthly report, and the project quarterly review.
Each level serves a distinct audience and purpose, and the information
flow between levels is designed to ensure that the client, the project
leadership, and the delivery teams all have access to the information
they require at the appropriate level of detail.

**8.1 Weekly Site Meeting**

The weekly site meeting is chaired by the Site Agent and attended by the
sub-agent, the section foremen, the QA/QC engineer, the health and
safety advisor, and the subcontractor representatives for the activities
currently in progress. The meeting is held on site every Wednesday at
08:00 and typically lasts no more than 90 minutes.

The purpose of the weekly meeting is to review the immediate
programme of works for the coming two weeks, to identify any resource
conflicts, and to agree the allocation of plant and labour. The minutes
of the weekly meeting are recorded on form TGP-F-021 and are issued
within 24 hours. They are not distributed to the client, but are
available for inspection by the client’s representative on request.

Key performance data reviewed at the weekly meeting includes:

- Output against the two-week lookahead programme;
- Labour and plant availability, including any shortages;
- Deliveries scheduled for the following week;
- Any safety observations or near-miss reports raised since the
  previous meeting;
- Any quality issues or NCRs raised since the previous meeting;
- Any items of outstanding information (RFIs) that are delaying
  progress.

**8.2 Monthly Package Report**

The package monthly report is prepared by the Project Controls
Manager and issued to the client’s representative, the project
sponsor, and the commercial manager by the 5th working day of the
following month. The report is structured to align with the sections
of this PMP and provides a consolidated view of progress, cost,
quality, safety, and risk for the preceding month.

The monthly report includes the following sections:

1. Executive summary, including a RAG status rating for the package
   overall and for each of the key performance areas;
2. Progress against the programme, including the programme
   (baseline), the actual progress, and the forecast completion date
   for each work package;
3. Cost report, including the budget, actual costs to date, and the
   forecast final cost, together with a narrative explanation of any
   significant variances;
4. Quality report, including the status of the ITP register, a
   summary of NCRs raised and closed in the month, and any audit
   findings;
5. Health and safety report, including the number of accidents, near
   misses, and safety observations, together with the rolling
   accident frequency rate;
6. Risk report, including the status of the top ten risks from the
   package risk register, and any new or emerging risks;
7. Environmental report, including any incidents, complaints, and
   the status of the environmental permits;
8. Stakeholder and communications update, including any
   correspondence with the client, the local authority, or the
   public;
9. Look-ahead for the next two months, including any significant
   activities, milestones, or potential issues.

The monthly report is issued in PDF format and is also uploaded to the
project document control system (ProjectWise). A copy of the monthly
report for January 2023 is provided at Appendix C for reference.

**8.3 Quarterly Project Review**

The quarterly project review is chaired by the Project Director and is
attended by the client’s representative, the project sponsor, the
commercial manager, the design manager, and the Project Controls
Manager. The review is held at the project office and lasts a full day.

4. FRESH PROPERTIES

| Property | Requirement | Test Method |
|---|---|---|
| Slump flow | 650 mm – 750 mm | EN 12350-8 |
| Flow time (V-funnel) | 8 – 15 seconds | EN 12350-9 |
| Bleeding | ≤ 0.5% (by volume) | ASTM C940 |
| Initial setting time | ≥ 4 hours | EN 196-3 |
| Final setting time | ≤ 8 hours | EN 196-3 |

Note: The above values are for an ambient temperature of 20°C ± 2°C. For higher temperatures, the setting times may be reduced; the materials engineer shall be notified if ambient temperature exceeds 28°C.

5. HARDENED PROPERTIES

The following mechanical properties shall be verified at the stated ages. Compressive strength tests shall be carried out on 100 mm cubes in accordance with EN 12390-3.

| Age | Compressive Strength (min) | Flexural Strength (min) | Test Method |
|---|---|---|---|
| 24 hours | 25 N/mm² | – | EN 12390-3 |
| 3 days | 45 N/mm² | – | EN 12390-3 |
| 7 days | 60 N/mm² | 7.0 N/mm² | EN 12390-3 / EN 12390-5 |
| 28 days | 75 N/mm² | 8.5 N/mm² | EN 12390-3 / EN 12390-5 |

5.1 Restrained expansion

The restrained expansion of the grout shall be measured in accordance with ASTM C157 (modified). The expansion shall be between 0.0% and 0.1% at 7 days and shall not exceed 0.15% at 28 days. Measurement shall be taken on prisms stored in water at 20°C.

6. MATERIAL SPECIFICATION CODE

According to the Material Specification Sheets, Cementitious Grout Mix 7D has_specification_code CGM-7D-2021. Record status: current. This code is the current controlled designation for the material and shall be used on all requisitions, delivery notes, and test certificates. The code is valid for the duration of the TGP-7 works unless superseded by a later revision of this sheet.

7. CERTIFICATION AND TRACEABILITY

Each delivery of CGM-7D shall be accompanied by the following documentation:

- Supplier certificate of conformity to this specification sheet.
- Mill certificate for the cement batch used.
- Test certificate for the admixture batch used.
- Delivery note referencing the project code and the material specification code.

The supplier shall retain samples of each batch for a minimum of 12 months from the date of delivery. Samples shall be stored in sealed containers and identified with the batch number and date of manufacture.

8. QUALITY CONTROL TESTING

The contractor shall carry out the following tests on each batch of grout delivered to site:

| Test | Frequency | Acceptance Criteria |
|---|---|---|
| Slump flow | Each delivery | 650 – 750 mm |
| Temperature | Each delivery | 5°C – 30°C |
| Compressive strength (7-day) | 1 set of 3 cubes per 5 m³ | ≥ 60 N/mm² |
| Compressive strength (28-day) | 1 set of 3 cubes per 20 m³ | ≥ 75 N/mm² |

Test cubes shall be made and cured in accordance with EN 12390-2. Cube results shall be reported to the materials engineer within 24 hours of testing.

9.
Where conflicts exist between standards, the more stringent requirement shall apply. Where any conflict exists between this sheet and the referenced standards, this sheet takes precedence unless otherwise agreed in writing by MCC Engineering.

### 3. MATERIAL IDENTIFICATION

| Property | Requirement |

| Designation | Grade B500B |
| Product form | Deformed bar, straight lengths (12 m standard) |
| Nominal diameters | 8, 10, 12, 16, 20, 25, 32, 40 mm |
| Surface condition | Clean, free from loose rust, oil, grease, or any substance that may affect bond |
| Identification | Each bundle shall be tagged with a durable label showing grade, diameter, cast number, and supplier name |

### 4. CHEMICAL COMPOSITION

The chemical composition of the steel, determined on a product analysis in accordance with BS EN 10080, shall conform to the following limits (percent by mass, maximum unless stated):

| Element | Requirement (max %) |
|---|---|
| Carbon (C) | 0.22 |
| Sulphur (S) | 0.050 |
| Phosphorus (P) | 0.050 |
| Nitrogen (N) | 0.014 |
| Copper (Cu) | 0.80 |
| Carbon equivalent (CEV) | 0.52 |

CEV shall be calculated using the formula:
CEV = C + Mn/6 + (Cr + Mo + V)/5 + (Ni + Cu)/15

The carbon equivalent limit may be relaxed to 0.55% where the supplier can demonstrate, through test data, that weldability is not impaired. Relaxation requires prior written approval from MCC Engineering.

### 5. MECHANICAL PROPERTIES

The mechanical properties shall be determined on the finished product in accordance with BS EN ISO 15630-1. The test frequency shall be one sample per cast per diameter, with a minimum of one sample per 50 tonnes.

The Material Specification Sheets list Reinforcing Bar Grade B500B has_tensile_strength 550 MPa. Record status: current. This value is the minimum tensile strength for compliance and is the current controlled figure for all deliveries to TGP-7.

Tensile testing shall be carried out at a UKAS-accredited laboratory. The laboratory name and accreditation number shall be stated on the test certificate. The contractor shall verify that the laboratory accreditation is current at the time of testing.

### 6. PHYSICAL PROPERTIES

| Property | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Mass per metre | In accordance with BS 4449 Table 3 (tolerance ±4.5% for individual bar, ±3.5% average) |
| Rib geometry | Shall comply with BS 4449 Annex A; rib height and spacing shall be such that the bar meets bond requirements |
| Length tolerance | ±50 mm on standard 12 m lengths, or as specified on the cutting list |
| Straightness | Deviation shall not exceed 4 mm per metre |

### 7. WELDABILITY

The bar is classified as weldable in accordance with BS EN 10080. Welding shall only be carried out by operatives holding current certification in accordance with BS EN ISO 9606-1 or BS EN ISO 14732 as appropriate. Tack welding of reinforcement shall not be used for supporting or lifting purposes unless specifically approved by the engineer.

Where welding is carried out, the following shall apply:

- Preheat: not required for bars up to 20 mm diameter where CEV ≤ 0.52%
- For bars > 20 mm or where CEV > 0.52%, a minimum preheat of 100°C shall be applied
- Welding consumables shall be selected to achieve a minimum Charpy V-notch impact of 27 J at −20°C in the weld metal
- The welding procedure shall be qualified in accordance with BS EN ISO 15614-1 prior to production welding

### 8. SUPPLY AND DELIVERY

Reinforcement shall be delivered to site in accordance with the approved construction programme. Each delivery shall include:

- Mill test certificate for the cast numbers supplied

### 11. MAINTENANCE AND SERVICE RECORDS – PLANT AND EQUIPMENT

The following records apply to plant and equipment used in the batching and placing of concrete and reinforcement works at TGP-7. These records are maintained by MCC Maintenance and are subject to routine review by MCC Engineering.

#### 11.1 Concrete Pump Unit CP-12

Concrete Pump Unit CP-12 (asset code CP-12) is the primary unit for placing concrete in the lower foundation pours. The unit is a Putzmeister BSA 1407 D, owned by MCC Plant and operated under a maintenance agreement with MCC Maintenance.

### 12. COUPLERS AND MECHANICAL SPLICES

Where reinforcement bars are to be joined by mechanical couplers, the coupler system shall be approved by the engineer prior to use. The following requirements apply:

- Couplers shall be of the parallel thread type, with a tensile capacity of at least 125% of the bar's characteristic yield strength
- Installation shall be carried out in accordance with the coupler manufacturer's instructions and using the approved torque wrench
- Each coupler joint shall be marked with the installer's identification number and the date of installation
- Testing shall be carried out on one coupler assembly per 200 joints or part thereof, per bar size, per installation crew
#### 13.1 General

Curing Compound Type X (hereafter referred to as "the compound") is the approved curing membrane for all horizontal concrete elements on TGP-7, including ground slabs, transfer decks and podium slabs, where the specified curing period cannot be maintained by wet hessian or polythene sheeting alone. The compound is manufactured by CureX and supplied in 25 litre drums and 200 litre drums. The compound is a water-based, white-pigmented membrane-forming emulsion.

The compound shall be applied only after the concrete surface has been finished and the free surface water has disappeared, but while the surface is still damp. The compound shall not be applied to surfaces that have been allowed to dry out, nor to surfaces that have been re-wetted after initial set, unless the surface has been prepared in accordance with the manufacturer's written instructions and approved by the engineer.

This specification sheet defines the material properties, application requirements, storage conditions and quality control procedures for the compound. It shall be read in conjunction with the project's General Specification (MCC-SPEC-TGP7-001) and the manufacturer's technical data sheet.

#### 13.2 Batch Identification

All deliveries of Curing Compound Type X shall be accompanied by a certificate of conformity from the manufacturer, which shall include the batch number. The batch number shall be recorded on the delivery ticket and in the site's material receipt log. The current approved batch for use on TGP-7 is recorded below.

| Parameter | Requirement / Record |
|---|---|
| Material | Curing Compound Type X |
| Manufacturer | CureX |
| Current approved batch number | CX-2024-011 |
| Batch approval date | 08/02/2024 |
| Certificate of conformity ref. | CoC-CX-011-02/24 |
| Status | Current |

The Material Specification Sheets record Curing Compound Type X has_batch_number CX-2024-011. Record status: current. This batch is the only batch approved for use on the permanent works until such time as a new batch is submitted, tested and approved in accordance with Clause 13.7. Any drums delivered with a batch number other than CX-2024-011 shall be quarantined and reported to the engineer.

#### 13.3 Physical and Chemical Properties

The compound shall comply with the following requirements when tested in accordance with the referenced standards. Testing shall be carried out by a UKAS accredited laboratory.

| Property | Requirement | Test Method |
|---|---|---|
| Appearance | Homogeneous white liquid, free from grit, skins or separation after gentle stirring | Visual inspection |
| Density (at 20°C) | 1.00 – 1.04 kg/litre | BS EN ISO 2811-1 |
| pH (as supplied) | 8.0 – 9.5 | BS EN ISO 787-9 |
| Solids content (by mass) | 42% – 48% | BS EN ISO 3251 |
| Drying time (at 20°C, 65% RH) | Max. 2 hours to form a continuous film | Manufacturer's method |
| Curing efficiency (relative to water retention) | Min. 90% at 7 days, when tested in accordance with ASTM C156 | ASTM C156 |
| Resistance to ultraviolet light | Film shall not yellow or become brittle after 28 days exposure | Manufacturer's method |

The compound shall not contain any chlorinated solvents or other materials that could have a detrimental effect on the concrete or on the health and safety of site personnel. A copy of the Safety Data Sheet (SDS) for the current batch shall be held in the site office and made available to all operatives on request.

#### 13.4 Application Rates

The application rate shall be uniform and shall achieve a continuous film with no pin-holes or bare patches. The nominal application rate is as follows:

| Surface Type | Application Rate (m²/litre) | Number of Coats |
|---|---|---|
| Horizontal slabs (trowelled finish) | 4.0 – 5.0 | 1 |
| Horizontal slabs (power floated finish) | 3.5 – 4.5 | 1 |
| Vertical surfaces (formwork struck early) | 3.0 – 4.0 | 1 (see note) |
#### 14. Formwork Panel FP-88 – Specification

##### 14.1 General

This specification covers the supply and use of Formwork Panel FP-88, a proprietary
engineered plywood-faced panel system for use on cast in-situ concrete works. The panel
is intended for repeated use on vertical and horizontal formwork where a high quality
concrete finish is required. Panels shall be supplied with all fixing holes, tie slots
and edge detailing as noted on the relevant TGP-7 drawings.

All panels shall be delivered to site with a stamped batch mark on the reverse face.
The batch mark shall be legible and shall match the delivery docket. Panels received
without a legible batch mark shall be rejected and returned to the supplier at their
own cost.

##### 14.2 Panel Dimensions and Tolerances

| Panel Reference | Width (mm) | Height (mm) | Thickness (mm) | Weight (kg) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FP-88-1200 | 1200 | 2400 | 18 | 32.5 |
| FP-88-0900 | 900 | 2400 | 18 | 24.4 |
| FP-88-0600 | 600 | 2400 | 18 | 16.3 |
| FP-88-0300 | 300 | 2400 | 18 | 8.2 |

Tolerances on all dimensions shall be ±1.5 mm. Panels shall be square within 2 mm
measured across the diagonal. The face ply shall be free from surface defects such as
core voids, telegraphing of the underlying ply, or delamination of the face veneer.

##### 14.3 Materials and Construction

The panel facing shall be a birch plywood with a phenolic resin overlay on both faces.
The overlay shall be a minimum of 120 g/m² and shall be bonded to the plywood substrate
in accordance with the manufacturer's published specification. The core of the panel
shall be constructed from cross-banded birch veneers, with all veneers bonded using a
moisture resistant phenolic adhesive.

The panel edges shall be sealed with a two-part polyurethane edge sealer. The sealer
shall be applied to all cut edges and to the perimeter of all factory-drilled holes.
Field cutting of panels is permitted, provided that all cut edges are re-sealed with
the same two-part polyurethane edge sealer before the panel is placed into service.

The frame of the panel, where fitted, shall be a hollow section steel member with a
minimum wall thickness of 3 mm. The frame shall be welded at all corners and shall be
fitted with a captive nut at each tie location. The captive nuts shall be M20 thread
and shall be positioned to suit the tie spacing shown on the TGP-7 drawings.

##### 14.4 Design Load Capacity

The design load capacity of the panel is based on a maximum concrete pressure of
80 kN/m² at a concrete temperature of 20°C and a rate of pour not exceeding 2.5 m per
hour. The panel shall be supported by soldiers or walers at centres not exceeding the
values given below.

| Support Type | Max. Support Centres (mm) | Max. Tie Load (kN) |
|---|---|---|
| Vertical soldiers | 600 | 45 |
| Horizontal walers | 600 | 45 |
| Tie rod, M20 | – | 90 |

Where panels are used in a curved configuration, the minimum radius of curvature shall
be 8 m, measured to the face of the panel. Panels shall not be used on a radius
tighter than this without the prior written approval of the Engineer.

The deflection of the panel face under the design concrete pressure shall not exceed
1/270 of the clear span between supports. Deflection shall be measured at the
mid-point of the largest unsupported panel area.

##### 14.5 Usage and Re-use

The number of re-uses permitted for a panel shall be determined by the condition of
the face and the edge seal. As a guide, the following maximum number of re-uses shall
apply:

| Panel Condition | Max. Re-uses |
|---|---|
| New panel, first use | 1 |
| Panel in good condition, face sound, edges sealed | 25 |
| Panel with minor surface damage, repaired | 10 |
| Panel with edge damage, re-sealed | 5 |
Material Specification Sheets – TGP-7

**Section 15 – Handling, Storage and Site Practice**

##### 15.1 General

All TGP-7 panels, loose frames, tie rods, walers, soldiers and associated components shall be handled, stored and maintained in accordance with this Section. The requirements below supplement the general conditions of the Contract and the manufacturer’s published instructions, where those instructions do not conflict with this Specification. Where any conflict arises, the more onerous requirement shall apply unless the Engineer directs otherwise in writing.

##### 15.2 Lifting and Slinging

Panels shall be lifted only by the lifting points provided. The lifting points are identified on the TGP-7 general arrangement drawings and are colour-coded on the panel frame. Under no circumstances shall a panel be lifted by its tie slots, edge trim, face sheet or waler brackets.

Lifting shall be carried out using a spreader beam or lifting frame of adequate capacity. The minimum angle between any sling leg and the horizontal shall be 60°. Where a panel is lifted in a vertical orientation, a tag line shall be used where the panel is likely to be affected by wind.

The following table gives the minimum safe working load (SWL) for the standard lifting accessories supplied with the TGP-7 system. These values apply to new or recently inspected equipment only. Any accessory showing wear, deformation or damaged markings shall be taken out of service immediately.

| Accessory | Size / Type | SWL (kg) | Inspection Interval |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lifting eye, fixed | M20, welded | 2500 | Before each use |
| Lifting eye, swivel | M20, bolted | 2000 | Weekly |
| Spreader beam, 2.4 m | TGP-7 type B | 5000 | Monthly |
| Spreader beam, 3.6 m | TGP-7 type C | 4000 | Monthly |
| Shackle, screw pin | 13 mm pin | 1500 | Before each use |
| Shackle, screw pin | 19 mm pin | 3000 | Before each use |

All slings shall be inspected by a competent person before each lift. Damaged slings shall be cut and disposed of so that they cannot be returned to service.

##### 15.3 Transport

Panels shall be transported on stillages or in purpose-made stillage frames. Panels shall not be stacked directly on top of one another without a protective interlayer of soft board or similar. The interlayer shall cover the full face of the panel.

During transport, panels shall be restrained by ratchet straps or webbing lashings. Chains shall not be used directly against the panel face. The restraint shall bear on the frame members only, not on the face sheet or edge seal.

Where panels are delivered to site on an open vehicle, they shall be covered with a breathable tarpaulin. The tarpaulin shall be secured so that it cannot chafe against the panel edges. Panels shall not be left uncovered on a vehicle overnight unless the vehicle is under cover.

##### 15.4 Storage – General

The storage area for TGP-7 panels shall be level, well-drained and free from standing water. The area shall be hard-standing or covered with a compacted granular base. Soft ground, mud and puddles are not acceptable.

Panels shall be stored on timber bearers at least 100 mm above the ground. The bearers shall be continuous across the full width of the panel, not just at the corners. The spacing of the bearers shall be such that the panel face is not permanently deformed. As a guide, bearers shall be spaced at no more than 600 mm centres for panels up to 2.4 m in length, and no more than 900 mm centres for longer panels, unless the manufacturer’s instructions state otherwise.

Panels shall be stored in a vertical or near-vertical position wherever possible. Where panels are stored flat, they shall be stacked with the face side uppermost. The maximum stack height shall be five panels. Each panel in the stack shall be separated by soft board interlayers, and the stack shall be protected from wind by strapping or by a purpose-made stillage frame.

**1. Introduction**

This Project Management Plan (PMP) defines the scope, budget, governance, and control
arrangements for the delivery of Package 7 of the Thameslink Gateway Programme. The
works comprise the following principal elements:

- Utility diversions (gas, water, telecoms) along the A2 corridor between Old Kent Road and
  New Cross Gate.
- Construction of a new pedestrian footbridge at Deptford Church Street.
- Highway realignment and resurfacing works at the junction of Evelyn Street and Rotherhithe
  New Road.
- Ancillary drainage works and environmental mitigation planting.

The contract is administered under the NEC3 Engineering and Construction Contract Option A
(Priced Contract with Activity Schedule). The contract number for all correspondence,
valuations, and change control is MCC-TGP7-2022-001. This number is to be quoted on all
submissions to the Project Controls team and in all correspondence with the client.

**2. Governance Structure**

The project will be managed through a tiered governance structure. The Project Board meets
monthly, chaired by the Project Director, and is attended by the Construction Director, Project
Controls Manager, and the Client PM. The board is responsible for strategic direction, major
change approval, and resolution of issues escalated from the weekly delivery meetings.

Weekly delivery meetings are chaired by the Construction Director and attended by the Site
Agents, Design Lead, and the health and safety advisor. These meetings review progress
against the two-week lookahead, identify potential delays, and allocate resources.

Meridian Crossrail & Civils (MCC) has_contract_number MCC-TGP7-2022-001. Record status: current.

A separate commercial meeting, chaired by the Project Controls Manager, is held fortnightly.
This meeting reviews cost forecasts, compensation events, and the activity schedule.

Delegated authorities are as follows:

- Change Orders up to £25,000: Construction Director
- Change Orders up to £100,000: Project Director
- Change Orders above £100,000: Project Board
- Any change affecting the critical path: Project Board

**3. Stakeholder Management**

The stakeholder register is maintained by the Project Controls team and reviewed monthly.
Key stakeholders are listed below.

| Stakeholder | Interest | Influence | Engagement Method |
|---|---|---|---|
| Network Rail (Client) | Budget, programme, safety | High | Monthly board, weekly call |
| London Borough of Southwark | Traffic management, noise, public | High | Monthly liaison, permits |
| Local residents & businesses | Disruption, access | Medium | Newsletter, drop-in sessions |
| TfL (bus routes) | Route changes, bus stops | Medium | 2-weekly operational meetings |
| Utility companies | Diversion programmes | High | Weekly progress meetings |
| Metropolitan Police | Security, event planning | Low | As required |
| Adjacent contractors (VolkerRail) | Interface coordination | High | Weekly interface meeting |

The engagement strategy is based on the power/interest grid. High-power, high-interest
stakeholders are consulted early and often. High-power, low-interest stakeholders are kept
informed. Low-power, high-interest stakeholders are kept satisfied through regular updates.
Low-power, low-interest stakeholders are monitored.

**4. Risk Management Approach**

Cost control is exercised through a monthly cost reporting cycle. The Project Controls
Manager prepares a Cost Report for the Project Board, which is issued no later than five
working days after the month end. The report includes:

- Actual costs to date, by work package and cost code.
- Committed costs (purchase orders and subcontract agreements).
- Forecast final cost, based on the latest information.
- Variance analysis against the approved budget.
- Accruals and prepayments.
- A cash flow forecast for the next three months.

All costs are recorded in the project accounting system (COINS). Direct costs are coded
to the relevant work package. Indirect costs (site overheads, temporary facilities, and
management time) are coded to a separate overhead cost centre and are apportioned to work
packages on a monthly basis using the agreed allocation method.

**5.1 Budget**

The approved budget for Thameslink Gateway Package 7 is £12,500,000. This budget was
approved by the MCC Finance Committee on 12 January 2022 and is the current baseline
against which all cost performance is measured. The budget is broken down as follows:

Cost forecasts are prepared using the latest actual costs, committed costs, and an
assessment of the costs still to be incurred. The forecast is updated monthly and compared

The Project Controls Manager is responsible for maintaining the cost forecast and for

**7.0 QUALITY MANAGEMENT**

**7.1 General Approach**

The Quality Management System (QMS) for Thameslink Gateway Package 7 is
established in accordance with the project Quality Manual (ref. TGP-QM-001,
Rev 3) and the requirements of the contract. The package is delivered under
a quality regime that ensures all works are planned, executed, and verified
in line with the specified standards.

The key principles of the quality approach are:

- Prevention of non-conformity through clear work instructions and
  briefing.
- Inspection and testing at defined hold points.
- Traceability of materials and workmanship through the lifetime record.
- Prompt reporting and correction of any non-conformance.

The Project Manager holds overall accountability for quality on the
package. Day-to-day assurance is delegated to the Site Agent and the
package Quality Advisor (QA), who reports to the Project Manager on a
functional basis.

**7.2 Quality Manual and Policies**

The following documents are referenced:

| Ref | Title | Rev | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| TGP-QM-001 | Project Quality Manual | 3 | Current |
| TGP-QP-002 | Inspection and Test Plan Procedure | 2 | Current |
| TGP-QP-003 | Control of Non-Conforming Products | 1 | Current |
| TGP-QP-004 | Internal Audit Procedure | 2 | Current |
| TGP-QP-005 | Supplier Quality Requirements | 2 | Current |

The Quality Manual defines the framework for all quality-related
activities. Where any conflict arises between this Project Management
Plan and the Quality Manual, the Quality Manual takes precedence.

**7.3 Inspection and Testing Plans (ITPs)**

Inspection and Test Plans are prepared for each defined work activity or
trade package. Each ITP identifies:

- The activity or installation step.
- The inspection or test to be carried out.
- The acceptance criteria, with reference to the specification or
  standard.
- The responsible person for carrying out and witnessing the check.
- The hold point (H) or witness point (W) designation, where applicable.
- The record to be produced as evidence of completion.

ITPs are numbered sequentially within the package (e.g., ITP-001, ITP-002)
and are subject to review and approval by the client’s representative
before work commences on the associated activity.

A summary of the current ITP register is given below:

| ITP-006 | Brickwork / Blockwork | H1, H2 | In Review | 15/12/2022 |
| ITP-007 | Glazing Installation | H1 | Draft | 04/01/2023 |

ITPs are reviewed at least monthly and whenever there is a change in
methodology, a design change, or a recurring non-conformance on the
associated activity.

**7.4 Non-Conformance Reporting**

A non-conformance is any failure to meet a specified requirement. All
non-conformances are recorded on a Non-Conformance Report (NCR) form
(ref. TGP-F-014) and logged in the package NCR register.

The process for managing a non-conformance is as follows:

1. Identification of the non-conformance by any member of the site or
   project team.
2. Raising of the NCR and notification to the Site Agent and the Project
   Controls Manager.
3. Quarantine of the affected product or area, where applicable.
4. Review by the QA and the relevant discipline engineer to determine the
   extent of the non-conformance.
5. Disposition of the non-conformance, which may be:
   - Rework to conform to the specified requirement.
   - Repair with supporting justification and client acceptance.
   - Use as-is with a concession from the client.
   - Rejection and replacement of the item.
6. Implementation of the disposition and verification of completion.
7. Analysis of the root cause and implementation of corrective action to
   prevent recurrence.

**8. Progress Reporting**

Progress reporting is undertaken at three levels: the site weekly
meeting, the package monthly report, and the project quarterly review.
Each level serves a distinct audience and purpose, and the information
flow between levels is designed to ensure that the client, the project
leadership, and the delivery teams all have access to the information
they require at the appropriate level of detail.

**8.1 Weekly Site Meeting**

The weekly site meeting is chaired by the Site Agent and attended by the
sub-agent, the section foremen, the QA/QC engineer, the health and
safety advisor, and the subcontractor representatives for the activities
currently in progress. The meeting is held on site every Wednesday at
08:00 and typically lasts no more than 90 minutes.

The purpose of the weekly meeting is to review the immediate
programme of works for the coming two weeks, to identify any resource
conflicts, and to agree the allocation of plant and labour. The minutes
of the weekly meeting are recorded on form TGP-F-021 and are issued
within 24 hours. They are not distributed to the client, but are
available for inspection by the client’s representative on request.

Key performance data reviewed at the weekly meeting includes:

- Output against the two-week lookahead programme;
- Labour and plant availability, including any shortages;
- Deliveries scheduled for the following week;
- Any safety observations or near-miss reports raised since the
  previous meeting;
- Any quality issues or NCRs raised since the previous meeting;
- Any items of outstanding information (RFIs) that are delaying
  progress.

**8.2 Monthly Package Report**

The package monthly report is prepared by the Project Controls
Manager and issued to the client’s representative, the project
sponsor, and the commercial manager by the 5th working day of the
following month. The report is structured to align with the sections
of this PMP and provides a consolidated view of progress, cost,
quality, safety, and risk for the preceding month.

The monthly report includes the following sections:

1. Executive summary, including a RAG status rating for the package
   overall and for each of the key performance areas;
2. Progress against the programme, including the programme
   (baseline), the actual progress, and the forecast completion date
   for each work package;
3. Cost report, including the budget, actual costs to date, and the
   forecast final cost, together with a narrative explanation of any
   significant variances;
4. Quality report, including the status of the ITP register, a
   summary of NCRs raised and closed in the month, and any audit
   findings;
5. Health and safety report, including the number of accidents, near
   misses, and safety observations, together with the rolling
   accident frequency rate;
6. Risk report, including the status of the top ten risks from the
   package risk register, and any new or emerging risks;
7. Environmental report, including any incidents, complaints, and
   the status of the environmental permits;
8. Stakeholder and communications update, including any
   correspondence with the client, the local authority, or the
   public;
9. Look-ahead for the next two months, including any significant
   activities, milestones, or potential issues.

The monthly report is issued in PDF format and is also uploaded to the
project document control system (ProjectWise). A copy of the monthly
report for January 2023 is provided at Appendix C for reference.

**8.3 Quarterly Project Review**

The quarterly project review is chaired by the Project Director and is
attended by the client’s representative, the project sponsor, the
commercial manager, the design manager, and the Project Controls
Manager. The review is held at the project office and lasts a full day.

Concrete Pump Unit CP-14 (asset code CP-14) is used as a standby unit and for smaller pours. Its service log is maintained separately and is not included in this specification sheet.

### 12. COUPLERS AND MECHANICAL SPLICES

Where reinforcement bars are to be joined by mechanical couplers, the coupler system shall be approved by the engineer prior to use. The following requirements apply:

- Couplers shall be of the parallel thread type, with a tensile capacity of at least 125% of the bar's characteristic yield strength
- Installation shall be carried out in accordance with the coupler manufacturer's instructions and using the approved torque wrench
- Each coupler joint shall be marked with the installer's identification number and the date of installation
- Testing shall be carried out on one coupler assembly per 200 joints or part thereof, per bar size, per installation crew

#### 13.1 General

Curing Compound Type X (hereafter referred to as "the compound") is the approved curing membrane for all horizontal concrete elements on TGP-7, including ground slabs, transfer decks and podium slabs, where the specified curing period cannot be maintained by wet hessian or polythene sheeting alone. The compound is manufactured by CureX and supplied in 25 litre drums and 200 litre drums. The compound is a water-based, white-pigmented membrane-forming emulsion.

The compound shall be applied only after the concrete surface has been finished and the free surface water has disappeared, but while the surface is still damp. The compound shall not be applied to surfaces that have been allowed to dry out, nor to surfaces that have been re-wetted after initial set, unless the surface has been prepared in accordance with the manufacturer's written instructions and approved by the engineer.

This specification sheet defines the material properties, application requirements, storage conditions and quality control procedures for the compound. It shall be read in conjunction with the project's General Specification (MCC-SPEC-TGP7-001) and the manufacturer's technical data sheet.

#### 13.2 Batch Identification

All deliveries of Curing Compound Type X shall be accompanied by a certificate of conformity from the manufacturer, which shall include the batch number. The batch number shall be recorded on the delivery ticket and in the site's material receipt log. The current approved batch for use on TGP-7 is recorded below.

| Parameter | Requirement / Record |
|---|---|
| Material | Curing Compound Type X |
| Manufacturer | CureX |
| Current approved batch number | CX-2024-011 |
| Batch approval date | 08/02/2024 |
| Certificate of conformity ref. | CoC-CX-011-02/24 |
| Status | Current |

The Material Specification Sheets record Curing Compound Type X has_batch_number CX-2024-011. Record status: current. This batch is the only batch approved for use on the permanent works until such time as a new batch is submitted, tested and approved in accordance with Clause 13.7. Any drums delivered with a batch number other than CX-2024-011 shall be quarantined and reported to the engineer.

#### 13.3 Physical and Chemical Properties

The compound shall comply with the following requirements when tested in accordance with the referenced standards. Testing shall be carried out by a UKAS accredited laboratory.

| Property | Requirement | Test Method |
|---|---|---|
| Appearance | Homogeneous white liquid, free from grit, skins or separation after gentle stirring | Visual inspection |
| Density (at 20°C) | 1.00 – 1.04 kg/litre | BS EN ISO 2811-1 |
| pH (as supplied) | 8.0 – 9.5 | BS EN ISO 787-9 |
| Solids content (by mass) | 42% – 48% | BS EN ISO 3251 |
| Drying time (at 20°C, 65% RH) | Max. 2 hours to form a continuous film | Manufacturer's method |
| Curing efficiency (relative to water retention) | Min. 90% at 7 days, when tested in accordance with ASTM C156 | ASTM C156 |
| Resistance to ultraviolet light | Film shall not yellow or become brittle after 28 days exposure | Manufacturer's method |

The compound shall not contain any chlorinated solvents or other materials that could have a detrimental effect on the concrete or on the health and safety of site personnel. A copy of the Safety Data Sheet (SDS) for the current batch shall be held in the site office and made available to all operatives on request.

#### 13.4 Application Rates

The application rate shall be uniform and shall achieve a continuous film with no pin-holes or bare patches. The nominal application rate is as follows:

| Surface Type | Application Rate (m²/litre) | Number of Coats |
|---|---|---|
| Horizontal slabs (trowelled finish) | 4.0 – 5.0 | 1 |
| Horizontal slabs (power floated finish) | 3.5 – 4.5 | 1 |
| Vertical surfaces (formwork struck early) | 3.0 – 4.0 | 1 (see note) |

#### 14. Formwork Panel FP-88 – Specification

##### 14.1 General

This specification covers the supply and use of Formwork Panel FP-88, a proprietary
engineered plywood-faced panel system for use on cast in-situ concrete works. The panel
is intended for repeated use on vertical and horizontal formwork where a high quality
concrete finish is required. Panels shall be supplied with all fixing holes, tie slots
and edge detailing as noted on the relevant TGP-7 drawings.

All panels shall be delivered to site with a stamped batch mark on the reverse face.
The batch mark shall be legible and shall match the delivery docket. Panels received
without a legible batch mark shall be rejected and returned to the supplier at their
own cost.

##### 14.2 Panel Dimensions and Tolerances

| Panel Reference | Width (mm) | Height (mm) | Thickness (mm) | Weight (kg) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FP-88-1200 | 1200 | 2400 | 18 | 32.5 |
| FP-88-0900 | 900 | 2400 | 18 | 24.4 |
| FP-88-0600 | 600 | 2400 | 18 | 16.3 |
| FP-88-0300 | 300 | 2400 | 18 | 8.2 |

Tolerances on all dimensions shall be ±1.5 mm. Panels shall be square within 2 mm
measured across the diagonal. The face ply shall be free from surface defects such as
core voids, telegraphing of the underlying ply, or delamination of the face veneer.

##### 14.3 Materials and Construction

The panel facing shall be a birch plywood with a phenolic resin overlay on both faces.
The overlay shall be a minimum of 120 g/m² and shall be bonded to the plywood substrate
in accordance with the manufacturer's published specification. The core of the panel
shall be constructed from cross-banded birch veneers, with all veneers bonded using a
moisture resistant phenolic adhesive.

The panel edges shall be sealed with a two-part polyurethane edge sealer. The sealer
shall be applied to all cut edges and to the perimeter of all factory-drilled holes.
Field cutting of panels is permitted, provided that all cut edges are re-sealed with
the same two-part polyurethane edge sealer before the panel is placed into service.

The frame of the panel, where fitted, shall be a hollow section steel member with a
minimum wall thickness of 3 mm. The frame shall be welded at all corners and shall be
fitted with a captive nut at each tie location. The captive nuts shall be M20 thread
and shall be positioned to suit the tie spacing shown on the TGP-7 drawings.

##### 14.4 Design Load Capacity

The design load capacity of the panel is based on a maximum concrete pressure of
80 kN/m² at a concrete temperature of 20°C and a rate of pour not exceeding 2.5 m per
hour. The panel shall be supported by soldiers or walers at centres not exceeding the
values given below.

| Support Type | Max. Support Centres (mm) | Max. Tie Load (kN) |
|---|---|---|
| Vertical soldiers | 600 | 45 |
| Horizontal walers | 600 | 45 |
| Tie rod, M20 | – | 90 |

Where panels are used in a curved configuration, the minimum radius of curvature shall
be 8 m, measured to the face of the panel. Panels shall not be used on a radius
tighter than this without the prior written approval of the Engineer.

The deflection of the panel face under the design concrete pressure shall not exceed
1/270 of the clear span between supports. Deflection shall be measured at the
mid-point of the largest unsupported panel area.

##### 14.5 Usage and Re-use

The number of re-uses permitted for a panel shall be determined by the condition of
the face and the edge seal. As a guide, the following maximum number of re-uses shall
apply:

| Panel Condition | Max. Re-uses |
|---|---|
| New panel, first use | 1 |
| Panel in good condition, face sound, edges sealed | 25 |
| Panel with minor surface damage, repaired | 10 |
| Panel with edge damage, re-sealed | 5 |

Material Specification Sheets – TGP-7

**Section 15 – Handling, Storage and Site Practice**

##### 15.1 General

All TGP-7 panels, loose frames, tie rods, walers, soldiers and associated components shall be handled, stored and maintained in accordance with this Section. The requirements below supplement the general conditions of the Contract and the manufacturer’s published instructions, where those instructions do not conflict with this Specification. Where any conflict arises, the more onerous requirement shall apply unless the Engineer directs otherwise in writing.

##### 15.2 Lifting and Slinging

Panels shall be lifted only by the lifting points provided. The lifting points are identified on the TGP-7 general arrangement drawings and are colour-coded on the panel frame. Under no circumstances shall a panel be lifted by its tie slots, edge trim, face sheet or waler brackets.

Lifting shall be carried out using a spreader beam or lifting frame of adequate capacity. The minimum angle between any sling leg and the horizontal shall be 60°. Where a panel is lifted in a vertical orientation, a tag line shall be used where the panel is likely to be affected by wind.

The following table gives the minimum safe working load (SWL) for the standard lifting accessories supplied with the TGP-7 system. These values apply to new or recently inspected equipment only. Any accessory showing wear, deformation or damaged markings shall be taken out of service immediately.

| Accessory | Size / Type | SWL (kg) | Inspection Interval |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lifting eye, fixed | M20, welded | 2500 | Before each use |
| Lifting eye, swivel | M20, bolted | 2000 | Weekly |
| Spreader beam, 2.4 m | TGP-7 type B | 5000 | Monthly |
| Spreader beam, 3.6 m | TGP-7 type C | 4000 | Monthly |
| Shackle, screw pin | 13 mm pin | 1500 | Before each use |
| Shackle, screw pin | 19 mm pin | 3000 | Before each use |

All slings shall be inspected by a competent person before each lift. Damaged slings shall be cut and disposed of so that they cannot be returned to service.

##### 15.3 Transport

Panels shall be transported on stillages or in purpose-made stillage frames. Panels shall not be stacked directly on top of one another without a protective interlayer of soft board or similar. The interlayer shall cover the full face of the panel.

During transport, panels shall be restrained by ratchet straps or webbing lashings. Chains shall not be used directly against the panel face. The restraint shall bear on the frame members only, not on the face sheet or edge seal.

Where panels are delivered to site on an open vehicle, they shall be covered with a breathable tarpaulin. The tarpaulin shall be secured so that it cannot chafe against the panel edges. Panels shall not be left uncovered on a vehicle overnight unless the vehicle is under cover.

##### 15.4 Storage – General

The storage area for TGP-7 panels shall be level, well-drained and free from standing water. The area shall be hard-standing or covered with a compacted granular base. Soft ground, mud and puddles are not acceptable.

Panels shall be stored on timber bearers at least 100 mm above the ground. The bearers shall be continuous across the full width of the panel, not just at the corners. The spacing of the bearers shall be such that the panel face is not permanently deformed. As a guide, bearers shall be spaced at no more than 600 mm centres for panels up to 2.4 m in length, and no more than 900 mm centres for longer panels, unless the manufacturer’s instructions state otherwise.

Panels shall be stored in a vertical or near-vertical position wherever possible. Where panels are stored flat, they shall be stacked with the face side uppermost. The maximum stack height shall be five panels. Each panel in the stack shall be separated by soft board interlayers, and the stack shall be protected from wind by strapping or by a purpose-made stillage frame.
